review: Radiation text, dose schedules, effect categories, shielding and treatment rows reviewed. Symptom inheritance, duration boundaries and cross-module trait consequences need independent validation before runtime completion.

entries.acceptance: At one or more accumulated rads, make the applicable health check, no more than once per day for continuing exposure to a given source; preserve source identity and current accumulated dose.
Use the table columns in critical-success, success, failure, critical-failure order; a no-obvious-effect outcome still leaves accumulated dose.
entries.validation_note: Pure whole-rad table and supplied-roll syndrome selection authored; 800-rad overlap blocked. Syndrome execution pending; fixtures unrun.

entries.acceptance: The supplied table prints both 161-800 and 800-4000 bands. Resolve the shared 800-rad endpoint explicitly before generating runtime ranges or asserting table completeness; do not silently choose a later-edition correction.
Outcome A begins after health hours, inflicts one die injury and gives low pain threshold for a week, or removes existing high pain threshold for that period.
After recovery from outcome A, make separate table-modified health checks for sterility and a one-year terminal condition; each occurs only on its own critical failure.

Outcome B includes A and, after health hours, nausea lasting forty minus health hours, independently rolled one-die losses to dexterity, intelligence and fatigue, plus impaired clotting; preserve the special recovery restrictions instead of assuming ordinary rest repairs these losses.
Each day make table-modified health checking: critical success restores two to each lost score, success one, failure none, and critical failure loses one more from each and adds nausea that day.
Once all B-related dexterity, intelligence and fatigue losses recover, remove its clotting impairment and daily recovery checks without deleting unrelated causes of those traits.
Outcome C includes B and adds hair loss and daily injury checks after half a die of weeks; until those injury checks stop, apply nausea and disease susceptibility -3.
For C daily health checks, critical failure inflicts one die injury, failure two, success one and critical success ends this injury process and enables normal recovery and hair regrowth.
If radiation injury exceeds two-thirds full health capacity, record the associated teeth and nail loss; preexisting nonradiation injury does not satisfy this trigger.
Outcome D includes C but begins health loss after half a die of days; critical success postpones loss only for that day and does not end the terminal process.
Outcome E begins after one hour, with separate one-die losses to dexterity, intelligence and fatigue, one die injury, impaired clotting, low pain threshold, disease susceptibility -3 and nausea.
Each E hourly health check causes immediate death on critical failure, two-point losses to each affected score and health on failure, one each on success, and no decline on critical success.
A single dose of at least two hundred rads causes sterility and blindness for one die of months in addition to other results.
A single dose of at least five hundred makes those sterility and blindness effects permanent.

At accumulated dose at least one hundred, a later parenthood event triggers a health check, with the source's male-parent +3 modifier; failure needs an authored offspring condition, not an arbitrary generated trait.
Apply species and individual radiation tolerance before selecting applicable biological effects; do not apply mammalian illness to every creature or machine.
Machines without electrical vulnerability are unaffected by these radiation rules.

For an electrically vulnerable machine, each newly accumulated hundred rads triggers health at +4 minus one per hundred accumulated rads; failure disables until repaired and critical failure destroys it and its stored data.
Divide received dose by protection factor from actual intervening shielding; preserve exposure geometry and distinguish protection from subsequent dose recovery.

entries.acceptance: At technology seven, a 500-unit preventive treatment taken one through three hours before exposure halves effective dose; it is not a retroactive eraser of absorbed radiation.
entries.implementation: Owned administration consumes one existing inventory dose, retains its timestamp, and halves new exposure from one through three hours afterward. The item provides the reference unit price; normal acquisition handles payment. Repeated overlapping administrations are rejected. Fixtures for boundaries, inventory, preview, rollback, undo and saved continuation are authored and unrun.

entries.acceptance: Technology-seven chelation costs 500, halves ongoing exposure from ingested fallout after three days and eliminates it after a week; already absorbed dose remains.
entries.implementation: Owned internal contamination and treatment records consume one appropriate inventory dose. Exact source fractions follow the three-day/seven-day basic schedule or twelve-hour advanced schedule. Authored instantaneous releases enter the shared received-dose ledger; zero releases retain receipts without adding doses. Existing absorbed dose is unchanged. Continuous exposure integration, repeated ingestion and repeat treatment remain unsupported. Boundary and persistence fixtures are authored and unrun.

entries.acceptance: Technology-nine treatment costs 1000 and grants +3 on radiation health checks for two weeks; overlapping administrations require explicit duration handling rather than unrestricted bonus stacking.
entries.implementation: RpgExpandedRadiationResistanceTreatment consumes one owned technology-nine dose and retains a two-week receipt. RpgExpandedRadiationContext adds three to radiation HT checks, with no dose removal. Overlapping courses are rejected. Fixtures for expiry, replay, rollback, undo and cross-process continuation are authored and unrun. Automatic syndrome and recovery procedures remain pending.

entries.acceptance: At technology ten or higher, an authored procedure may repair radiation injury completely while the patient is alive; specify which dose, symptoms and permanent changes it reverses.
For one through ten rads, modifier zero and ordered outcomes none, none, A, B.
For eleven through twenty rads, modifier zero and outcomes none, A, B, C.
For twenty-one through forty rads, modifier zero and outcomes A, B, C, D.
For forty-one through eighty rads, modifier -1 and outcomes A, B, C, D.
For eighty-one through 160 rads, modifier -3 and outcomes A, B, C, D.
The printed 161-800 band has modifier -4 and outcomes A, B, C, D; its upper endpoint conflicts with the next row.
The printed 800-4000 band has modifier -5 and outcomes C, D, E, E; resolve its overlapping lower endpoint explicitly.
Above 4000 rads, modifier -5 and outcomes D, E, E, E.
Baseline cosmic exposure is one rad per week before applicable shielding.
Fallout within a few hours can deliver two through five rads per minute; the author specifies dose rate and duration.
Over the following day fallout can deliver several rads per hour; ingestion creates a separate continuing internal source.
A nearby reactor accident can deliver at least one thousand rads per hour, divided by squared distance in yards; zero-distance handling requires a finite defined source geometry.
Ingested material creates a persistent isotope-specific rate from roughly one rad daily to several per minute; separate toxic effects may also apply.
A radiation-modified innate attack delivers one rad per point of rolled damage, before applicable radiation protection.
The listed one-megaton fission air/space-burst example at two thousand yards delivers 6600 rads; do not extrapolate a complete blast model from this single example.
Half an inch of lead gives protection factor two.
One and a half inches of steel gives protection factor two.
Seven hundred fifty yards of air gives protection factor two.
One yard of water gives protection factor eight.
One yard of earth gives protection factor twenty-seven.
One yard of concrete gives protection factor sixty-four.

exclusions.reason: Exclude source prose and narrative context. Retain fictional-game hazard rates and mechanics as neutral implementation requirements; these are not real-world exposure guidance.
